text:
maya: FYI — payments put enterprise account ACME-8901 on a payment hold this morning after some anomalous activity. Need to gather dispute evidence and a timeline so we can decide whether to escalate to collections or release the hold.

payments-bot: Payment hold created for account ACME-8901 by payments-team at 2025-10-03T09:12:01Z. Reason: multiple PM declines + sudden 10x usage spike.

tom: Confirmed. Hold was auto-triggered by the fraud rules after 3 declined card attempts + 4 large refunds in same billing period. I pulled the initial invoice list: INV-2025-09-2112, INV-2025-09-2113, INV-2025-09-2114, INV-2025-09-2115.

sasha: Can you paste the specific timestamps and amounts for those invoices and any merchant gateway IDs? We need that to cross-check against gateway logs and the customer's support tickets. Also we should note whether any of these were disputed at the bank level.

tom: Quick copy: 
- INV-2025-09-2112 — $48,120 — paid 2025-09-30T14:03Z (card ending 4242)
- INV-2025-09-2113 — $51,000 — attempted 2025-10-01T02:11Z (declined)
- INV-2025-09-2114 — $49,300 — chargeback filed 2025-10-01T05:23Z (gateway id gw_78df)
- INV-2025-09-2115 — $46,700 — paid 2025-10-01T07:02Z

Use this export to fetch raw records: 
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $BILLING_KEY" "https://billing.redwood.ai/exports/ACME-8901?run=latest" > /tmp/acme-8901-invoices.json
```

liam: Customer support got an email at 09:16 from a security contact claiming they didn't authorize the spike. Forwarded transcript to billing. They said teams spun up integration keys using an IP range we don't usually see.

maya: Okay — action items: (1) revenue ops needs invoice + gateway IDs (tom provided), (2) eng/infra needs IP + API key audit logs, (3) legal needs the copy of any customer emails / PO and decision on whether to pause service entirely. Please attach evidence to the shared S3 folder below.

tom: Uploaded a redacted billing export to s3://redwood-evidence/ACME-8901/2025-10-03/charges-redacted.csv (link expires 30d). Also dropped the gateway dispute ticket: https://payments-gw.example/tickets/gw_78df.

sasha: Thanks. Maya, do we have the API access log snippet for the spike window (2025-09-29 23:00 to 2025-10-01 08:00 UTC)? We need to correlate IPs and any new keys created. If keys were created from the customer's SSO, that changes the story.

maya: Eng-infra asked me to request the exact request-ids. They gave this query to run: 
```
SELECT request_id, api_key_id, src_ip, user_agent, timestamp
FROM api_access_logs
WHERE account_id = 'ACME-8901' AND timestamp BETWEEN '2025-09-29' AND '2025-10-01';
```

aisha: Legal here — for us to support a fraud claim we need: signed PO (if available), original billing emails, the customer email claiming unauthorized use, gateway dispute docs, and any proof of service showing the customer received outputs (to counter a wrongful-dispute claim). Also note chain-of-custody for logs (who exported what and when). If the customer used SSO and an internal user created keys, that looks like internal compromise, not fraud.

liam: I uploaded the customer's support transcript to the same S3 path: s3://redwood-evidence/ACME-8901/2025-10-03/support-transcript.txt (redacted). Customer says their security team will provide a brief incident report by EOD.

sasha: Recommend interim posture: keep account on hold for billing operations but allow read-only API calls (no model execution) so the customer can access historical data. Minimizes business impact but prevents additional charges. Thoughts?

aisha: I support read-only temp access but require documented approval from the customer's security contact before we re-enable writes. Also request a signed letter from their procurement if they want account re-enabled pending dispute resolution.

tom: OK — I've set metadata tag hold_reason=payment_dispute, hold_owner=billing, and noted the requested evidence in the ticket. I'll also flag the largest invoices for collections review if we don't get a response in 10 business days.

payments-bot: Account ACME-8901 remains on hold (hold_owner=billing). Next automatic review scheduled 2025-10-13T09:12:01Z.

maya: Thanks everyone. I'll assemble a timeline + checklist and DM the cross-functional folks. Please drop any more artifacts in the S3 folder and reply here when done.

sasha: ack :thumbsup:

liam: pinged customer for the incident report, they said security will send it before EOD PST.

ops-bot: Note added to account: "evidence_in_progress" by maya at 2025-10-03T09:30:12Z.

maya: If we get the incident report and gateway docs within 48 hours, we'll kick off a fraud review with collections and legal to determine whether to issue chargebacks or release.

tom: will update ticket when gateway responds.

aisha: If anyone gets direct proof of internal compromise (SSO logs showing unknown user), escalate immediately to legal and security.

sasha: Understood — keeping this thread as the single source of truth for evidence collection.

maya: closing loop — thanks all.
